title: Laws of UX Review
subtitle: Annotated findings for a SaaS pricing page fixture

findings.observation: Four equal hero actions compete for the first decision.
findings.recommendation: Keep one primary action and demote the rest to links.
verification: Only one hero action has primary visual weight.

findings.observation: Every plan uses the same emphasis, so the recommended option is not distinctive.
findings.mechanism: A visually distinct item is more likely to be noticed and remembered.
findings.recommendation: Give one evidence-backed recommendation a distinct treatment.
verification: A five-second recall check identifies the recommended plan.

findings.observation: Nine peer features appear as one uninterrupted group.
findings.mechanism: Chunking reduces the amount of information held as separate items.
findings.recommendation: Group related features under three descriptive headings.
verification: Every feature belongs to one clear group and the groups scan independently.

findings.observation: The completed flow ends with a generic thank-you and no next action.
findings.mechanism: The ending disproportionately shapes the remembered experience.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the achieved outcome and offer one relevant next step.
verification: The completion state names the outcome and exposes one next action.
